newsitem.title: USA: NGC to buy Destec Energy for about $1.3 billion.
newsitem.headline: NGC to buy Destec Energy for about $1.3 billion.

text.p: NGC Corp., jockeying to become a major player in the nation's rapidly restructuring electric power industry, agreed on Tuesday to acquire independent power producer Destec Energy Inc. for about $1.3 billion in cash.
In negotiations that stretched into the early morning hours, Houston-based NGC beat out 30 bidders vying for Destec and its interests in 24 power plants, executives said.

As state and federal legislators weigh breaking utilities' monopoly control over electric power grids, independent power marketers are buying up generating assets in the hope of forming nationwide franchises.

NGC plans to retain Destec's U.S. power operations, spin off $407 million of its international power projects to AES Corp., and sell another $300 million in non-strategic assets in the deal, executives said.
"It looks like a third of (Destec) is what we will end up with and that's what we were interested in," NGC Chairman Chuck Watson said.

Dow Chemical Co., which controls more than 80 percent of Destec shares, agreed to the $21.65-a-share deal, which is expected to receive federal regulatory approval and close in the second quarter, the companies said.
Destec, formed as a Dow Chemical subsidiary in 1989 to produce electricity and steam for U.S. industrial customers, was later spun off as a public company.

The Houston-based company put itself up for sale after losing contracts accounting for a third of its revenue and 700 megawatts of capacity when two Texas utilities terminated power contracts in 1994 and 1995.

Destec's gas-fired power plants fit well with NGC's gas production and transmission system, but analysts said the profitability of the deal could hinge on whether electric prices are pulled lower by competition in the years ahead.

"Strategically, I think it is a good deal," said Petrie Parkman & Co. analyst Stuart Wagner. "The concern has got to be as power generation comes under pressure, as the price of electricity comes down, will it be (a good deal) in a couple of years?"

NGC coveted Destec's generating capacity to build up its ability to offer one-stop shopping for industrial customers seeking natural gas and electric power and as a base for its foray into a deregulated electric market.
"(The acquisition) really positions us to be an unquestioned leader in the deregulation of the electric business over the next several years," Watson said.
NGC last year sold 15 million megawatt hours into the domestic wholesale electric market, making the company one of the top five wholesalers in the United States.
NGC shares were down unchanged at $19.75 a share in New York Stock Exchange trading, and Destec shares were up $1 at share at $20.50 on the Big Board in late-afternoon trading.
